Table 9: Paired Wilcoxon tests across ten seeds. Positive pairs count seed-wise improvements of the deployed INT8 model over the FP32 baseline.
Table 10: Paired intrinsic-XAI comparison: qZACH-ViT + RASO minus qZACH-ViT + Adam + Lattr.

Figure 1: Mean paired change of the actual ONNX INT8 qZACH-ViT models relative to the FP32 ZACH-ViT baseline. Error bars are 95% confidence intervals across the ten seed-wise differences within each dataset.
Figure 5: Mean fraction of RASO training batches with a negative classification-attribution gradient inner product. Error bars show variation across epochs and seeds.
Figure 4: Selected source-model intrinsic-XAI metrics normalized within each metric for visualization. Raw values and statistical tests are reported in Table 4 and Appendix C.2.

Table 5: Same-model source-XAI comparison on qZACH-ViT + RASO. Each row summarizes 1,200 matched explanations. Patch occlusion is both an explainer and the reference for Occ. ρ, so its value of 1 is tautological.
Table 8: Secondary binary test metrics, mean ± standard deviation over ten seeds.
Table 6: Architecture and actual serialized deployment size. Sizes are MiB. Reduction is relative to the corresponding serialized source checkpoint.

Figure 3: Serialized size and CPU latency normalized independently to the corresponding source value. The actual INT8 ONNX artifact is 70.0% smaller, and end-to-end inference is 1.41 times and 2.39 times faster with one and four threads, respectively.
Figure 8: Intrinsic maps from the three source qZACH-ViT conditions for the same OCTMNIST image. The visual difference is descriptive; no anatomical localization target is available.

Figure 7: Matched XAI methods for one OCTMNIST test image and one source qZACH-ViT + RASO checkpoint. The original and overlay are shown for each method. The model predicts class 3 while the true class is 2.
